samples.summary: Batch happy-path content assertions read the optimistic cache, not the CRDT — a batch whose writes never landed would still pass
samples.evidence: The new `batch()` tests assert content with `store.getBlock(...)`/`store.getDocument()` on the same store instance (e.g. "one undo reverts every write in the batch": `expect(store.getBlock(block.id)!.inlines...).toBe('hello world')` before undo). `YorkieDocStore.getDocument()` returns `this.cachedDoc` when `!this.dirty` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:611-613), and every write path sets `this.cachedDoc = currentDoc` optimistically regardless of whether the Yorkie change committed. The whole point of this diff is that batched writes go through an ambient `activeRoot` instead of their own `doc.update` — the exact path where a write could be built against a discarded/stale context and silently dropped. This file already has the correct pattern for such an assertion (`new YorkieDocStore(doc).getBlock(...)`, used in the 'rethrows' test and the 'applyStyle attribute removal' block), but none of the happy-path batch tests use it. Undo-stack length +1 only proves *a* change was pushed, not that all three writes were in it.

samples.summary: Nested-batch test asserts only the undo-unit count; it never checks the nested body's write was applied
samples.evidence: `it('a nested batch does not open a second undo unit')` performs `store.applyStyle(..., { italic: true })` inside an inner `store.batch(...)` and then asserts only `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length === before + 1`. If the nested fast path (`if (this.activeRoot) { fn(); return; }` plus `withUpdate` reusing `activeRoot`) dropped or misrouted the inner write entirely, the undo-stack count would be unchanged and the test would still pass. No assertion on `italic` after the batch, and none through a fresh store. The MemDocStore nested test (packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts) has the same shape: it only asserts the post-undo text, never that the nested `'?'` insert landed first.

samples.summary: MemDocStore: the documented "on a throw the partial writes stand and the checkpoint is kept" behaviour is untested
samples.evidence: memory.ts:204-212 keeps the checkpoint on a throw specifically so partially-applied writes remain undoable. The only throw test ('re-arms snapshotting after the batch ends, even on a throw') has a body that writes *nothing* before throwing, so `wroteNothing` is true and the checkpoint is popped — the kept-checkpoint branch is never exercised. A test that writes then throws, then undoes back to the pre-batch document, is missing.

samples.evidence: `skipNonHistoryPresence()` is consulted at two call sites: `publishResolvedLocalCursor` (line 1228) and `updateCursorPos` (line ~3151). Nothing calls `publishResolvedLocalCursor` inside a batch, so the second site's skip — and its early `return` now bypassing the presence publish — has no coverage.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no happy-path batch test reads the CRDT, so dropped batched writes would go undetected. Two counterexamples exist. (a) yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:804-818: after two batches, `store.undo()` sets `dirty = true; cachedDoc = null` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2897-2902), so line 817's `store.getBlock(...)` bypasses the optimistic cache (getDocument's cache branch at 611-613 is skipped) and re-parses the Yorkie tree; asserting 'first' pins that batch #1's insertText actually landed in the CRDT. The same applies to the post-undo reads at 707-709. (b) editor-undo-selection.test.ts:280-304 drives `editor.updateStyleToMatch` against a real yorkie.Document; that path runs inside `docStore.batch()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1080-1088, 2933-2959) and writes `root.stylesJson` through the ambient root (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2810-2816), while the assertions at :287/:299 use `store.getDocStyles()`, which reads `this.doc.getRoot().stylesJson` with no cache at all (yorkie-doc-store.ts:644-652, 691-693). A batch whose writes were discarded would fail both. The narrower point that the pre-undo assertion at line 704 reads the warm cache is true but is not an uncovered behavior, so it is not blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified both cited tests and the code under test. yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:712-724 asserts only `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length === before + 1` after a nested batch containing `applyStyle(..., { italic: true })` — no assertion that the italic write landed (nor via a fresh store). memory.test.ts:255-269 asserts only the post-undo text 'Hello' and `canUndo() === false`, so the nested `insertText(block.id, 6, '?')` is never checked. Both assertions hold if the nested fast path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2861-2864 `if (this.activeRoot) { fn(); return; }` with withUpdate at :2840-2848; memory.ts:176-188) dropped or misrouted the inner body entirely. I searched wide for a counterexample: a multiline grep for batch-inside-batch across all *.test.ts finds no other docs-store nesting; packages/docs/test has no other `batch(` usage; the only production docs caller of batch() is withNamedStyleChange (docs/src/view/editor.ts:1080-1092), which does not nest and whose suite (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:244-321) exercises only a top-level batch; the docs concurrent integration file and tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts contain no batch calls. The closest analogue that DOES assert the nested write (packages/notes/src/store/memory.test.ts:47-58, `expect(s.getText()).toBe('abc')`) is a different store class in the notes package and exercises none of the docs-store code. So a nested-batch regression that silently loses a write would ship undetected — a real, in-lane coverage gap over new behavior.
